title: A Visitor for the Room
premise: Elodie Lockridge returns to the family farmhouse to bury their twin brother Wren, only to find that everyone in town remembers a funeral for Elodie instead. The house's mirrors begin lagging one second behind reality, and in that stolen second, something else moves through the rooms — something that has been counting the Lockridges, one per generation. As Elodie documents the haunting like testimony, they realize the entity is a ledger of debts: the family survived a fire decades ago by letting someone else burn. To get their found family out alive, Elodie must give the count what it is owed before it finishes tallying — and at the climax, they offer themselves as the missing entry, breaking the cycle by finally naming the forgotten victim aloud. The mirrors catch up; the survivor walks out of the house carrying the record, justice served outside any court.
about_author: N. M. Vane is the pen name of a former county archivist who spent years cataloguing unclaimed estates and the paperwork of the dead. They write horror about records, grief, and the arithmetic of survival from a farmhouse with suspiciously old mirrors.

chapters.title: The Wrong Name on the Stone
chapters.summary: Elodie arrives home to bury Wren but finds their own name carved into the headstone. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread as the town greets them with condolences meant for a ghost.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Haunted House
chapters.summary: Elodie begins documenting the house room by room, a coping ritual turned investigation. Their cousin Marisol and Marisol's daughter Birdie arrive seeking shelter. POV: Elodie. Beat: fragile warmth forming around shared damage.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: Elodie notices the hallway mirror reflects movement a beat late — a hand raising after their hand has lowered. POV: Elodie. Beat: the first undeniable proof, quiet terror replacing skepticism.

chapters.title: What Birdie Saw
chapters.summary: Seven-year-old Birdie describes 'the counting man' who stands in her doorway tallying on his fingers. Adults dismiss it until she draws him perfectly. POV: alternating Elodie and Marisol. Beat: parental fear fusing the found family tighter.

chapters.title: The Fire Ledger
chapters.summary: In the attic, Elodie finds a 1960s insurance file: the Lockridge house burned, and a hired hand named Tobias Vetch was never accounted for among survivors or dead. POV: Elodie. Beat: guilt surfacing — the family's survival had a price someone else paid.

chapters.title: Condolences for the Living
chapters.summary: At the wake, neighbors behave as if Elodie died years ago; an old woman whispers that the house 'takes its turn.' POV: Elodie. Beat: isolation deepening, the town complicit in forgetting.

chapters.title: Reflections Out of Order
chapters.summary: Every mirror now lags, and in the delay Elodie sees figures: Vetch, burned, mouthing numbers. The lag widens to two seconds. POV: Elodie. Beat: documentation becomes desperate evidence-gathering.

chapters.title: Marisol's Bargain Instinct
chapters.summary: Marisol wants to flee immediately; Elodie insists on finishing the record first. Their argument cracks the household. POV: Marisol. Beat: love expressed as conflict — flight versus witness.

chapters.title: The Count Begins
chapters.summary: Birdie goes briefly missing and is found inside a mirror-frame's shadow, reciting numbers up to four. Four Lockridges remain. POV: Elodie. Beat: the abstract threat acquires a body count and a deadline.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Tape
chapters.summary: A cassette reveals Great-Aunt Hester confessing: during the fire, the family barred the servants' door so their own would live. Vetch was behind it. POV: Elodie. Beat: inherited sin made explicit; shame and fury.

chapters.title: Two Seconds Gone
chapters.summary: The lag stretches; whole minutes vanish. Elodie loses an afternoon and wakes with ash on their sleeves. POV: Elodie. Beat: the house is consuming time itself, and Elodie is being edited out.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot
chapters.summary: Elodie searches county archives for Vetch's grave and finds every record of him redacted or burned — erased even from paper. POV: Elodie. Beat: righteous anger; documentation meets institutional erasure.

chapters.title: Birdie Counts to Five
chapters.summary: Birdie adds a fifth number and names it 'the lady in the glass' — a previous victim. The entity has been collecting across generations. POV: Marisol. Beat: scope widens; maternal terror becomes resolve.

chapters.title: Exodus Attempted
chapters.summary: The family packs to leave, but the road loops back to the house; the property won't release its debtors. POV: Marisol. Beat: despair — escape is impossible while the count stands unfinished.

chapters.title: The Rule of Substitution
chapters.summary: Elodie deciphers the pattern in Hester's notes: the count can be satisfied by a named offering, but only if the forgotten are remembered first. POV: Elodie. Beat: hope kindled inside horror — memory as weapon.

chapters.title: Naming the Dead
chapters.summary: Elodie performs a rite of testimony, reading Vetch's reconstructed life aloud in every mirrored room. The reflections stop lagging — then all turn toward them. POV: Elodie. Beat: awe and peril; attention is not safety.

chapters.title: The Counting Man Comes Downstairs
chapters.summary: Vetch manifests fully, patient and terrible, holding out five fingers. He does not want revenge; he wants to be counted. POV: Elodie. Beat: confrontation stripped of violence, more chilling for its calm.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Elodie offers themselves as the sixth entry to close the ledger and free the others. Marisol refuses; Birdie, unexpectedly, says the man 'just wants his name back.' POV: Marisol. Beat: sacrifice reframed — maybe no one must die.

chapters.title: Written Into the Record
chapters.summary: Elodie carves Vetch's full name beside the family's on a new stone and reads the complete account into the house itself. The mirrors shatter outward. POV: Elodie. Beat: climax — truth as exorcism, at real cost: Elodie's reflection stays behind.

chapters.title: Sixth Entry, Closed
chapters.summary: The house exhales; the loop breaks. But Elodie casts no shadow now, and the town suddenly remembers both twins' funerals. POV: Elodie. Beat: victory with a wound — survival priced in permanence.

chapters.title: Leaving the Door Open
chapters.summary: The found family departs together, taking the archive with them. Elodie vows to testify for other erased dead. POV: Marisol. Beat: tenderness; justice continues beyond the haunted ground.

chapters.title: A Visitor for Every Room
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Elodie receives photographs of mirrors lagging in strangers' homes, each with a name attached. The work has only begun. POV: Elodie. Beat: ominous resolve — the price of survival is becoming its keeper.
